publishes: q_actual -- the trajectory after the physics pass

scene.name: seat
scene.provenance: derived -- fitted to the commanded pose: soles on the floor puts the pelvis origin at 0.5929 m; its underside, 0.1475 m lower, is where the seat top goes. It reaches to x=-0.038, carved back until no leg link ever comes within 0.064 m of it -- and is 0.060 m thick, not a block to the floor, and 5 mm clear of the pelvis because a pinned robot needs scenery, not a contact

scene.name: cup
scene.collision: none -- the object is animated, not simulated. A kinematic body here cost 9.52 deg of tracking RMSE against 0.165 deg without it, because nothing closes the hand on it and the body ends up inside the hand
scene.provenance: derived -- the right hand's grasp centre -- the midpoint of the palm and the middle fingertip, so the object is where a closed hand would hold it -- over frames 20-83, the span from the first hold to the last. Outside it the object rests on its surface at the pick-up and put-down positions

scene.name: dining table
scene.collision: disabled -- scenery, see the placement report
scene.provenance: derived -- its top is solved for the target, not taken from the catalog: the cup rests at 0.7468 m, so the surface is at 0.7125 m. The catalog's 0.75 m at scene scale would be 0.5137 m -- the same rule the seat follows, and the two agree to 0.199 m. Footprint at the one scene scale, oriented with its near edge across the reach, pulled back 0.000 m and lowered 0.000 m. No height clears the reach -- the hand is inside the plane the object rests on, by 22 mm at worst on 10 frames of the approach and the withdrawal -- so the surface is scenery: geometry with its collider disabled. Nothing rests on it but an object the hand carries kinematically, and the overlap is the reach's to fix

placement.rule: physical consistency, then the task, then the image -- the design's priority order, applied in that sequence

hand_contact.by: construction -- the handled object is placed on the hand

placement.link_collision_boxes: 46 links, from the asset's own collision bounds

built.root_z_why: seated invariant: pelvis sits at the seat top with the thigh horizontal

invariants.name: seated
invariants.evidence: median knee flexion 109 deg over all 96 frames
requires: the pelvis rests on a support surface (+/- 0.02 m)
both soles stay on the floor (+/- 0.02 m)
invariants.seat_why: soles on the floor puts the pelvis origin at 0.5929 m; its underside, 0.1475 m lower, is where the seat top goes. It reaches to x=-0.038, carved back until no leg link ever comes within 0.064 m of it -- and is 0.060 m thick, not a block to the floor, and 5 mm clear of the pelvis because a pinned robot needs scenery, not a contact
invariants.breaks_if: the seat keeps its human-scale catalog height, or the physics pass is allowed to drop the root to the floor

invariants.name: hand_contact
requires: the acting hand is within 2 cm of the handled object for every hold frame
invariants.breaks_if: the reach is matched in joint angles only -- the G1's arm is shorter than the subject's, so equal angles land the hand short

scene_scale.why: seat 0.3082 m (solved for the G1) over catalog 0.450 m -- hip axis at knee height 0.3526 (shank 0.3176 + sole 0.0350); seat top one thigh half-thickness (0.0444) below it; pelvis origin 0.2573 above it

scene.how: how far the image-derived position is from the hand that holds it -- the object is placed on the hand (priority 2) and this is what that costs against the image (priority 4)
scene.note: the gap is in the retarget's arm direction, not in the placement: the waist carries no chest rotation, so a reach to the subject's side comes out as a reach to the robot's front

scene.how: the trajectory takes the object at one height and sets it down at another; the surface goes under the lower of the two so the object never penetrates it, which leaves the pick-up starting this far above it
how far the object moves on the frame the hand takes it -- the closest this trajectory brings the hand to the object where it rests
a support surface is solved for the target; the catalog height at scene scale is what it would have been

how far the acting arm reaches inside the surface it reaches over, with every link at the radius of its own collision mesh -- a reach defect, which is why the surface is scenery rather than a collider
how far the surface had to drop below the height the object rests at, so the reach that takes the object does not pass through it
no robot link is inside a leg on any frame
acting hand's grasp centre to the handled object, over every hold frame
scene.note: satisfied by construction: the object is placed on the hand. What it does not say is whether the hand is where the subject's was -- that is `scene.<object>.image_vs_hand`

definition.synthesized: authored by the adapter to keep the target consistent
definition.unavailable: nothing filled it -- a defect, not an outcome

derived.rule: leg joints solved so the soles reach the floor the contact mask asserts
placed on the acting hand's grasp centre: the phase signal says it is held, and an object that is held is where the hand is
the surface under the handled object: its height from where that object rests, its footprint at the scene scale
